title: Profile cache
brief: The profile page shows old display names for a long time after users change them, and under load the database gets hammered with the same query. The cache is supposed to keep the newest profiles and expire them after a minute. Read the code and find out why it does not behave that way.

issues.why: popitem(last=True) removes the most recently used entry. The cache throws away exactly what it should keep. The second test in test_cache.py would fail.
issues.good_fix: popitem(last=False) removes the least recently used entry, because get() and put() move keys to the end.

issues.why: Updating an existing key keeps the old expiry, so a value that is rewritten often can still expire early, and a refreshed value does not get a fresh minute.
issues.good_fix: Compute a new expires_at on every put, including updates.

issues.why: Many threads miss at once and all call the database for the same user (a stampede). OrderedDict is not safe for concurrent get/put/move_to_end, and the lock in update_display_name guards nothing the readers use.
issues.good_fix: Put one lock inside TTLCache around every operation. For the stampede, use a per-key lock or in-flight marker so one thread loads and the others wait for its result.

issues.why: update_display_name edits the cached dict in place. Readers that already hold the same dict see it change mid-use, and a profile that has expired is never refreshed.
issues.good_fix: Delete the cache entry after the database write (or store an immutable value and replace it), so the next read loads fresh data.

extension: Add a get_or_load(key, loader) method to TTLCache that never runs the loader twice at the same time for the same key, and does not cache a loader failure.
